question.text: This empire located in the Indian subcontinent was founded by Babur. Shah Jahan who built the Taj Mahal, was a ruler of this empire.
question.clue: Nadir Shah defeated this empire at the Battle of Karnal.

swap.text: When she declared a state of emergency, Indira Gandhi and her son Sanjay spearheaded a population control strategy in which poor men and women were forced to undergo this medical procedure.
swap.answerHtml: sexual sterilization (accept word forms like sterilize; accept male and/or female sterilization; accept vasectomy or tubectomy)

question.text: After he murdered Mahatma Gandhi, Godse was put on trial in the Red Fort of this Indian city. A "New" district of this city is the capital of India.
question.clue: Plans for George VI to impress the "native minds" of this city by traveling to it via plane to hold a grand ceremony at Coronation Park were dropped because of their lack of political or financial tact.

swap.text: Rajendra Chola also defeated this island's kingdom of Anuradhapura. Arab merchants monopolized this island's city of Colombo to trade with its Sinhalese kingdoms.
swap.answerHtml: Sri Lanka [or Ceylon; or the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; or Ilangai Jananayaka Socialisa Kudiarasu; or Sri Lanka Prajatantrika Samajavadi Janarajaya]
swap.clue: It got one of its former names from the city Kandy.

question.text: Afonso de Albuquerque conquered this city on India's west coast in 1510. It remained a Portuguese possession until India annexed it in Operation Vijay.
question.clue: Much later, this state became part of a union territory along with the exclaves of Daman and Diu on the coast.

swap.text: This foreign leader ordered the RAW ["R-A-W"] to help train and arm Bangladeshi insurgents. The assassination of this Indian leader led to the launch of Operation Blue Star.
swap.clue: The "Smiling" Buddha nuclear test was conducted under this leader, who ruled through executive decree and suspended civil liberties during a period known as the "Emergency."

question.leadin: This king's name literally means "without pain," which is ironic given the cruelty for which he was known early in his life.
question.text: Name this third Maurya emperor and son of Bindusara. He is famous for his Rock Edicts and namesake pillars.
question.clue: Some monuments created by this man were inscribed in Brahmi, others were inscribed in Greek.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the cartoons of Thomas Nast.
swap.text: In order to attack Catholicism, Nast depicted an upside-down American flag, ruins of a public school, poor, defenseless protestant schoolchildren, and crocodiles with bishop hats for snouts on the banks of an "American" version of this river.
swap.clue: The iron-rich Magadha kingdom along this river's banks gave birth to a dynasty ruled by Nanda.

question.leadin: Name these nineteenth-century conflicts involving Britain.
question.text: This 1857 revolt in India was allegedly brought on by the cartridges for the new Enfield rifles being greased with pork and beef fat.
question.clue: The notoriously bloody Siege of Cawnpore took place during this event, which was triggered by a new Enfield cartridge that used animal fats as grease, thus offending both Hindus and Muslims.

swap.leadin: This dynasty reached its peak in the 9th century AD before being overthrown by the Pandyan Dynasty in the 1300s, ending a 1600 year period of rule over South India.
swap.text: The Brihadisvara is one of which dynasty's "Great Living Temples" that it built in its capital of Thanjavur? During the height of its power, it established a maritime empire stretching from the Philippines to the Maldives.
swap.clue: This dynasty conquered the Andaman and (+) Nicobar Islands under Rajendra I, son of Raja Raja I. This dynasty originates from the Sangam Period, as do the Chera and Pandya dynasties.

question.leadin: This empire's ruler Rajaraja the Great built the Brihadisvara temple, dedicated to Shiva.
question.text: Rajaraja the Great ruled this empire which extended influence over much of the eastern Indian Ocean. Rajaraja and his successor Rajendra led this empire during its successful invasions of Sri Lanka and the Srivijaya kingdom.
question.clue: This empire's defeat of the Sailendra dynasty in Palembang was chronicled in inscriptions at the Brihadishvara Temple in this empire's capital of Thanjavur.

swap.text: This soldier led the British forces at Plassey. He had earlier successfully taken and held Arcot through a siege by Chanda Sahib, an action that caused Pitt the Elder to describe him as the "heaven-born general."
swap.clue: The definitive biography of this man is H.H. Dodwell's, which contrasts him to his French counterpart, Joseph Dupleix.

question.leadin: A prime minister from this family was deposed by a military council during Operation Fair Play.
question.text: Since its 1967 founding, leadership of the PPP party has been held by the Zadaris and what other family? In 1988, a member of this family became the first woman to be elected head of government of a Muslim-majority country.
question.clue: One member of this family famously stated that his government would "eat grass" if it would help obtain nuclear weapons.

swap.text: This colony provided much of the manpower for Britain's attack on German East Africa, comprising the majority of the forces in the early battles of Kilimanjaro and Tanga. After the war, forces largely drawn from this colony fought in the Third Anglo-Afghan War.
swap.clue: Lord Curzon established this colony's North-West Frontier Province, whose western border was set at the Durand Line to settle the Great Game with Russia.

question.leadin: This polity was once led by the female ruler Razia, and it began to decline as a result of the rise of Vijayangara [vij-ya-na-GA-ra].
question.text: Name this empire of northern India whose Khalji dynasty fought off an invasion by the Chagatai Khanate and whose last ruler was defeated at the Battle of Panipat.
question.clue: This polity's ruling dynasties included the Burji and Khilji, and rulers of this polity including Balban were former slave soldiers known as ghulams.

swap.text: Both Harper and the UK House Foreign Affairs Committee cited the human rights violations of this Sri Lankan president who used heavy-handed tactics to end his country's long-running civil war.
swap.clue: The Tamil Tigers were defeated in 2009 under the leadership of this President of Sri Lanka who suffered a shock defeat in the 2015 presidential election to Maithripala Sirisena.

question.leadin: Answer the following about violent events in the lead-up to Indian independence.
question.text: A spate of politically-motivated assassinations followed after Lord Curzon announced this 1905 territory-changing action, which was more limited in scope than a similar 1947 action accompanying Indian independence.
question.answerHtml: Partition of Bengal [accept synonyms, accept descriptive equivalents, like the creation of West and East Bengal]

swap.text: The anti-Mughal alliance led by Rana Sanga is often referred to as a "confederacy" of these "princes" who ruled a number of Hindu states before the Muslim conquests of the northern subcontinent.
swap.clue: An entire ruling family of these people called the Guhilas was wiped out in 1303 after the capture of the Chittor Fort.

question.text: The Mysorean ruler Hyder Ali reprimanded his admiral, Ali Raja, for blinding the sultan of this place. Operation Cactus intervened in a much later coup attempt in this territory.
question.clue: In the 20th century, this country was long led by the dictator Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who sparked civil unrest in 2005 by arresting the main opposition figure, Mohamed Nasheed.

swap.leadin: Charles Boone commissioned a "floating castle" ship to defeat this empire's naval officer Kanhoji Angre, but failed when that ship, the HMS Phram, caught fire.
swap.text: Name this empire primarily ruled by a peshwa. This empire's first chhatrapati ("CHUH-truh-puh-tee") established its first capital at Raigad.
swap.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.
